# Setup

## Prerequisites

- A SLURM cluster, or one machine with enough memory for the `hic` step
  (see [Cluster Reference](cluster.qmd))
- `python3` >= 3.11 and `conda` >= 24.7.1, loaded by your site's
  `profiles/<site>/env.sh`. A one-time Miniforge install in
  `$HOME/miniforge3` works on every cluster; set `MICROC_CONDA_ROOT` if it
  lives elsewhere. See [Cluster Reference](cluster.qmd#conda-version).
- Paired-end Micro-C FASTQ files (`.fastq.gz`)
- A genome FASTA indexed for BWA (`bwa index genome.fa`), and a chromosome
  sizes file

There is no separate setup script: environments are built by Snakemake the
first time a rule needs them. The juicer_tools jar ships in `scripts/`.

## 1. Samplesheet

`MicroCSamplesheet.txt` is tab-separated, one row per **sequencing run**
(one pair of FASTQ files). A library sequenced on two lanes has two rows.

| Column | Contents |
|--------|----------|
| `Name` | A label for the row (required, but not used in file names) |
| `Read1`, `Read2` | FASTQ file names |
| `Sequencing_Directory` | Folder that holds both files (joined with the file name) |
| `Seq_Rep` | Sequencing replicate number (required column) |
| every column in `mergeBy` | e.g. `Project`, `Cell_Type`, `Bio_Rep`, `Tech_Rep` |
| anything else | metadata (`Condition`, ...) |

```
Name                Project  Cell_Type  Condition  Bio_Rep  Tech_Rep  Seq_Rep  Read1                  Read2                  Sequencing_Directory
GM12878_ctrl_1_1_1  Example  GM12878    Ctrl       1        1         1        MicroC_2M_R1.fastq.gz  MicroC_2M_R2.fastq.gz  /path/to/raw/
```

The columns in `mergeBy` are joined with `_` to name the **group**, the
unit that gets one set of outputs (`Example_GM12878_1_1` above). Rows with
the same group name are one library: their runs are aligned separately and
then merged and deduplicated together. With the default
`mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep', 'Tech_Rep']`, `Seq_Rep` is not
part of the name, so sequencing replicates merge into one library. Add
`Seq_Rep` to `mergeBy` to keep them as separate groups.

::: {.callout-warning}
Group names become folder and file names, and are inserted into a pattern
Snakemake uses to match files. Use letters, digits and underscores only in
the `mergeBy` columns, and avoid values that make two groups look alike.
:::

### Merge samplesheet

`MicroCMergeSamplesheet.txt` (used only by the Merge workflow) has the
`mergeBy` columns plus `pairs`: the path to a Core `.pairs.gz`.

```
Name                Project  Cell_Type  Condition  Bio_Rep  Tech_Rep  pairs
GM12878_ctrl_1_1    Example  GM12878    Ctrl       1        1         output/Example_GM12878_1_1/Example_GM12878_1_1.pairs.gz
GM12878_ctrl_1_2    Example  GM12878    Ctrl       1        2         output/Example_GM12878_1_2/Example_GM12878_1_2.pairs.gz
```

Its `mergeBy` is `merge: mergeBy:` in the config (by default without
`Tech_Rep`, so these two rows become one group, `merged_Example_GM12878_1`). Relative
paths are relative to the folder you launch from; if you set
`MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT`, give the full path to the Core output.

## 2. Reference

Both are paths in the config.

- `fasta`: the FASTA passed to `bwa mem`; its BWA index files
  (`.bwt`, `.pac`, `.sa`, ...) must sit next to it.
- `chromSizes`: two columns, chromosome name and length, with the **same
  names as the FASTA**. Every contig listed becomes part of the maps, so
  trim the file to the chromosomes you want. One way, for a UCSC-style
  hg38 FASTA:

```bash
samtools faidx genome.fa
grep -E '^chr([0-9]+|X|Y|M)\s' genome.fa.fai | cut -f1,2 > hg38.chrom.sizes
```

Set `genome` (default `hg38`) to the assembly label recorded in the
`.cool` files.

## 3. Config

Edit `config/MicroCConfig.yaml`. The fields most runs change:

| Field | What to set |
|-------|-------------|
| `samplesheet`, `mergeBy` | Samplesheet path and grouping columns |
| `outputDir` | Where outputs go (default `output`; relative paths go under `$MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT` if set) |
| `genome`, `fasta`, `chromSizes` | Reference |
| `outputs` | Any subset of `cool`, `mcool`, `hic` |
| `base_resolution`, `resolutions`, `hic_resolutions` | Bin sizes |
| `javaMem` | Optional JVM heap for the `hic` step (default: 85% of the rule's memory) |
| `qc_thresholds` | Pass / warn / fail cut-offs for the dashboard |
| `analysis` | Optional downstream analysis |

See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for every key.

## 4. Compute site

Pick your site's profile folder: `profiles/biowulf`, `profiles/longleaf`,
`profiles/pioneer`, `profiles/local` (no scheduler), or your own copy of
`profiles/slurm-template`. The config default is `profiles/local`. On a
cluster, set it once in `~/.bashrc`, together with where output should go:

```bash
echo 'export MICROC_PROFILE=profiles/biowulf' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT=/data/$USER/MicroCPipe' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

See [Cluster Reference](cluster.qmd#per-cluster-settings). Also open the
profile's `config.yaml` and check the account and partition are yours.

## 5. Conda environments

Each rule runs in one of four environments in `envs/` (`microc_align`,
`microc_cooler`, `microc_hic`, `microc_qc`), which Snakemake builds on first
use. Building them inside the launcher job needs more memory than a login
node; build them once on a compute node before the first real run:

```bash
srun -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 --mem=16g -t 3:00:00 --pty /bin/bash   # add -p <partition>
bash MicroCPipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only
exit
```

The channels are conda-forge and bioconda; set
`conda config --set channel_priority strict` if the build complains about
conflicts. Editing an env file gives it a new hash, so Snakemake builds a
fresh environment; delete the old one under `.snakemake/conda/` to free
space.

## 6. Email (optional)

```bash
export MICROC_EMAIL=you@university.edu   # e.g. in ~/.bashrc
```

You then get one email when a run starts, finishes, or fails. See
[Running](running.qmd#email-notifications) for the `notify:` options.

## 7. Check the setup

Before submitting hundreds of jobs, list them:

```bash
bash MicroCPipe.sh -n
```

A dry run reads the samplesheet and config, checks the input files exist,
and prints every job it would run. It runs no tools. See
[Running](running.qmd#dry-run-first).

## Troubleshooting setup

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `... is missing column(s): [...]` | Header typo, or spaces instead of tabs | Use tabs and the exact column names |
| `resolution N is not a multiple of base_resolution` | A resolution the base does not divide | Use multiples of `base_resolution` |
| `config 'outputs' has unknown format(s)` | Typo in `outputs` | `cool`, `mcool`, `hic` |
| `MissingInputException` naming a FASTQ | `Sequencing_Directory` or file name wrong | Check the path on this cluster |
| `bwa` reports it cannot open the index | The FASTA has no BWA index next to it | `bwa index genome.fa` |
| `Error running conda info` | conda not on `PATH` | Fix the conda line in `profiles/<site>/env.sh` |
| Launcher `OUT_OF_MEMORY` on the first run | Environments built inside the launcher job | Build them once on a compute node (step 5) |
